title: Runtime Eval Orchestration — Architecture Sync (notes)
content:
Meeting: Runtime Eval Orchestration architecture sync
Date: 2024-11-05 10:00-11:00 PT
Location: Zoom / #eng-runtime
Attendees: Priya Nair (owner), Ethan Morales, Kai Zhang, Lina Patel, Diego Ramos, Sophie Laurent

Purpose:
- Align on the design for the Eval Orchestration subsystem: how the runtime will schedule, run, and consume automated evaluation runs across model variants, quantization profiles, and caching strategies. Goal is to produce a concrete RFC-ish sketch we can iterate on before EOD Fri.

TL;DR decisions:
- We will introduce a lightweight "eval-controller" service that owns scheduled evaluation workflows (not a monster workflow engine).
- Leverage existing rollout APIs for model pinning and automatic fallback; eval-controller will post candidate verdicts but not directly mutate routing without a human-approved rule.
- Store eval definitions as YAML blobs in model-artifact store (signed) and reference them from the model manifest.
- Use spot/backfill GPU workers for heavy offline evals; lightweight online quality checks run on warm dedicated slots.

Notes / Discussion:
1) Motivation and scope
- Current problem: ad hoc eval scripts in PRs and local runs; no standard orchestration, results scattered across S3 and spreadsheets. Hard to compare quantized vs FP results across prompt-sets.
- Scope for first phase: scheduled nightly batch evals across a curated set of prompt-sets + fast smoke checks on rollouts. Not building full CI replacement.

2) Controller responsibilities (sketch)
- Read EvalDefinitions (YAML) that declare: model_variant, quantization_profile, prompt_set_id, metrics to collect, timeout, resource_class.
- Enqueue jobs into the existing runtime job-queue with labels for affinity (gpu_type, seq_len).
- Aggregate results, compute deltas vs baseline, store normalized artifacts (JSON metrics + artifacts link).
- Emit an evaluation summary event to observability and create a Jira ticket when thresholds regress.

3) Data storage and provenance
- Keep signed EvalDefinition blobs alongside model artifacts (reuse artifact-signing flow). This ensures reproducible eval runs.
- Results stored in eval-store bucket with metadata index (keyed by model_version, eval-id, timestamp). Keep TTL for raw logs (90 days) and longer for summaries (2 years).
- Action: Lina to draft the metadata schema for eval results (fields to include, minimal required). Due 2024-11-12.

4) Runtime integrations
- Worker selection: small batch jobs should prefer dedicated inference slots (warm KV cache). Nightly sweeps with long sequences use spot pools and enable KV warmup stages.
- Cost control: add a per-eval cost cap and automatic cancellation if projected token cost exceeds budget.

5) Rollouts and safety
- Eval-controller verdicts are advisory. Decision flow: eval summary -> human reviewer -> if approved, call rollout API to adjust routing weights.
- For canary rollback automation, allow an "auto-fail" flag on critical metrics; auto-fail only triggers a rollback to previous stable variant and only for safety-critical customers (explicit opt-in).

6) Observability and alerts
- Emit standardized events for start/complete/fail with correlation IDs to link to trace spans.
- Create a per-model dashboard that surfaces latest eval run, 7-day trend, and top failed prompts.

7) Security and compliance
- Eval jobs on private deployments must use customer VPCs and respect model data residency. Eval-controller should support a mode where results never leave customer VPC (deferred work for phase 2).

Design alternatives discussed (pros/cons):
- Heavyweight workflow engine (Airflow/Argo) vs small controller + existing job-queue: We prefer controller for faster iteration and lighter operational overhead. If we need complex DAGs later, we can integrate with Argo.
- Store eval definitions in Confluence vs artifact store: artifact store wins for provenance and signing. Confluence can be used for human-facing docs.

Action items (owners + rough eta):
- Lina Patel: Draft eval result metadata schema and sample JSON mapping. Due 2024-11-12.
- Diego Ramos: Prototype eval-controller minimal API (create/list/run) + local runner shim. Due 2024-11-19.
- Kai Zhang: Instrument rollout API to accept advisory-eval-tokens and attach eval metadata to rollout events. Due 2024-11-15.
- Ethan Morales: Setup experimental nightly eval job in test cluster and wire basic dashboard panels. Due 2024-11-22.
- Priya Nair: Write short RFC (one-pager) capturing the decisions here and the compatibility constraints (artifact signing, storage TTL, access controls). Draft due 2024-11-08. Final RFC by 2024-11-13.

Open questions / unresolved:
- How do we surface prompt-level failure triage to non-engineers? (product/CS UX)
- Should eval-controller attempt lightweight repro prompts when a regression is detected or just capture state and leave repro to an engineer? Tradeoff between automation vs noisy retries.
- Exact cost-budgeting model for large-scale nightly runs; do we enforce global budget or per-team budgets? Need finance input here.

Quick design snippet (informal YAML idea):
---
# EvalDefinition example (informal)
name: nightly-llama-quant-check
model_variant: llama-70b-v2
quant_profile: q4_0
prompt_set_id: release-smoke-2024-11
metrics:
  - name: exact_match_ratio
    threshold: 0.92
  - name: latency_p95
    threshold: 350ms
resource_class: small-gpu-warm
schedule: cron(0 3 * * *)
notify: ["#eng-runtime", "eval-notifications@redwood.com"]
retain_summary_days: 720
---

Notes to self / follow-up for RFC: include a short example of the eval summary JSON and reference implementation snippets for the job payload. Also propose a small schema migration for the model manifest to include eval-patterns reference.

Meeting adjourned 11:00. Minor sidebar on model-artifact signing cadence (Sophie to sync with platform-engineering next week).

notes_brief: Architecture sync to design a lightweight eval-controller for scheduling and aggregating model evaluation runs across quantization and cache strategies. Decision: controller + job-queue with advisory rollouts; store EvalDefinitions in artifact store; prototype work assigned.
